preamble: Debuccalization of the voiceless palatal stop [c] to the glottal fricative [h] is a defining innovation of the Timbira languages (Northern Jê) of Brazil: Proto-Northern Jê *c became *h in Proto-Timbira (and was lost before *w), so that Parkatêjê, Canela, Krahô and Pykobjê have h wherever Mẽbêngôkre and Apinajé have a glottal stop or zero and Panará has s. Proto-Akuwẽ (Central Jê) shows the same change, but only before *i.

languageExamples.language: Proto-Northern Jê to Timbira (Parkatêjê, Canela, Pykobjê)

examples.note: Forms in Nikulin's Macro-Jê alphabet: c = voiceless palatal stop or coronal affricate, ĵ = its voiced counterpart, ñ = [ɲ], y = [ɨ ~ ɯ], ə̂ = [ɘ ~ ɤ], ô/ê = close-mid vowels.

examples.to: Parkatêjê hək, Canela hək, Pykobjê hək

examples.note: Wiktionary lists Apinajé and Mẽbêngôkre jaê, without the consonant.
Practical orthography: c = [k]. Tapayúna katuwa and Apinajé kaur show the other branches' reflexes.
Before *i only; elsewhere *c stays c (Proto-Akuwẽ *kuci 'boil', Xavánte ʔuci).

sources: Nikulin, A. (2020). Proto-Macro-Jê: um estudo reconstrutivo. https://repositorio.unb.br/handle/10482/38893
